problem: Deep RL agents need millions of episodes to learn vision-language-action tasks and it is unclear whether they can implicitly decompose and recompose concepts (e.g. color and shape) to generalize to unseen combinations or more complex out-of-distribution tasks.
motivation: Children learn individual concepts first, and this speeds up later compositional learning. The paper tests whether the same pretraining order (concept learning, then compositional learning) helps RL navigation agents, and whether pretrained vision-language text encoders help.
key_idea: Pretrain an RL navigation agent on single-attribute (color OR shape) invariance tasks, then train it on color-shape composition. This speeds up learning and enables zero-shot generalization to complex three-word compositions, and a CLIP text encoder further helps.
insight: Concept learning (C|S) followed by composition (C&S) reaches the criterion 100x (train) and 20x (test) faster in the composition phase, and it is the only recipe that transfers zero-shot to C&S&S (reward about 5.5, versus -5.10 and -23.2 for C&S-only at 67.4K and 168.6K episodes). PCA of LSTM activity shows the concept-pretrained agent uses a larger representation space (7 PCs vs 3 for 90% variance). Among text encoders, only vision-grounded CLIP helps; text-only BERT fails on test combinations, so grounding matters.
method: Unity synthetic 3D environments: room with 4 spawn locations, 5 shapes x 5 colors. C&S (color+shape target), C&S&S (color plus two shapes, test-only OOD), C|S (single-word color or shape, forces invariance), C*&S (5 extra unseen colors).
Train/test split: 20 color-shape combos for training and 5 held-out diagonal combos for compositional testing. C&S&S has its own split with 'familiar' and 'unseen' combinations.

Agent: 3-conv vision module (3136-D) plus language module (one-hot vectors for color and shape, 128-D linear), concatenated into a 256-D mixing layer, then LSTM, then actor (4 actions) and critic; trained with A2C and RMSProp (lr 2.5e-4).
Curriculum: concept learning on C|S (about 168K episodes), then compositional learning on C&S. Compared against C&S from scratch and against a C&S checkpoint matched for total episodes.

Text-encoder variants: one-hot, vanilla (CLIP tokenizer + trainable embedding), frozen BERT, frozen CLIP, each projected to 128-D. Evaluated on train/test episodes-to-criterion and on zero-shot novel colors (C*&S).
Reward and criterion: +10 for reaching target, -3 for hitting a wrong object, -1 for hitting a wall, -10 at 500 steps. Criterion is average reward >= 9 over 100 episodes.

setting.backbone: Small CNN + LSTM actor-critic with one-hot / vanilla / frozen BERT / frozen CLIP text encoders (trained from scratch with A2C)
setting.training_data: RL episodes in custom Unity environments (about 67K-200K episodes per training stage); CLIP and BERT pretrained and frozen; no other data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 128x128 plus text instruction (one-hot or string)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move forward, move backward, turn left, turn right

numbers.method: C&S one-hot from scratch (episodes to criterion, K)
numbers.extra: N=3 seeds; metrics are thousands of episodes to reach avg reward >=9; Test = held-out combinations
pretrained on C|S for about 168K episodes first; the K episodes reported are for the C&S phase only
numbers.evidence: Table 1: C|S -> C&S 0.6 ± 0.1 train, 5.5 ± 2.9 held-out test

numbers.method: CLIP text encoder agent (episodes to criterion, K)
numbers.backbone: frozen CLIP text encoder + CNN-LSTM A2C

numbers.evidence: The agent achieves a noteworthy zero-shot result, averaging 6.9 over three repeats

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; results are on the authors' custom Unity environments, with episodes-to-criterion and average reward as metrics.
results: RL agents learn to compose held-out color-shape combinations (about 67K train / 95K test episodes). Concept pretraining cuts the compositional phase to 0.6K/5.5K episodes, and only that agent transfers zero-shot to C&S&S (reward about 5.5). A CLIP text encoder beats one-hot (56.2K vs 67.4K) and reaches reward 6.9 on 5 unseen colors, while BERT fails on test combinations.
limitations: Very simple environments: basic shapes, 5 colors, fixed room, no obstacles, instructions of only 2-3 words, so generalization to realistic scenes is unproven.
Concept-learning benefit tested only with a one-hot agent and a from-scratch visual encoder; pretrained visual encoders were not tested. Only 3 seeds.
builds_on: Hill et al. grounded language agent (2020)
